title: Agents on the Canvas in tldraw — Steve Ruiz, tldraw
talk_summary: Steve Ruiz demos tldraw's experiments putting AI agents visually on a shared canvas: single-shot structured-output drawing, then an agentic loop, then multiple 'fairy' agents that see each other's work, elect a leader, and delegate a to-do list. The most concrete orchestration lesson is a leader/follower pattern with shared state and explicit non-overlap, plus a local desktop app exposing an HTTP endpoint that executes posted JavaScript so agents can script the app.

takeaways.technique: Leader election + delegated to-do list over shared state
takeaways.what_they_do: When several agents are grouped on one task, one is elected leader; it scouts current state, writes a to-do list, and delegates items to the other agents, then observes and judges completion rather than doing the work itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: one of them will be elected leader... it's going to go scout kind of what's going on on the canvas, and then it's going to create a to-do list, and it's going to delegate that to-do list to the other agents

takeaways.technique: Shared visible state to prevent blind overlap
takeaways.what_they_do: Agents can see each other's in-progress actions on the canvas, so concurrent agents avoid working on the same region; the speaker frames the core problem as agents being 'essentially blind while they're working'.
takeaways.evidence_quote: how do we manage the fact that these things are essentially blind while they're working? And prevent them from kind of overlapping

takeaways.technique: Local app exposing an execution endpoint to agents
takeaways.what_they_do: They wrapped the app in Electron and opened an HTTP port where anything POSTed is executed as JavaScript, deliberately trading safety for maximal agent agency in a local, file-based context.
takeaways.evidence_quote: anything that gets posted to that endpoint, uh treat it as JavaScript and run it. Which is a terrible idea.

takeaways.technique: Structured-output tool calls instead of image generation
takeaways.what_they_do: The drawing agent emits text structured outputs that invoke the same primitives a human uses (shapes, circles) rather than generating pixels, which sidesteps conflicting vision training data.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It is using text structured outputs to to make the same things that I could make, right? So, I have I have tools.
